angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 201,753 km at 99.14 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.0872 +/- 0.0241 mas (same row, RUWE 1.09): 99.14 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.29 +/- 0.06 solar radii from Adams et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-137 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract): 201,753 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.463 +/- 0.052 solar masses from Smith et al. 2018, the stellar mass of K2-137 b's parameter set from Smith et al. 2018 (the default leaves it empty) in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018MNRAS.474.5523S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3697 +/- 109 K from Adams et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-137 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Adams et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-137 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021PSJ.....2..152A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-137.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 5.179, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
